transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2025-08-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Sofia (ACME CTO), Liam (ACME ML Eng), Harpreet (ACME Infra), Nina (ACME Product)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on migrating from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated. Primary drivers: cost predictability, data residency, control over runtimes (vLLM/TGI compatibility), and eval parity for prompt behavior. Raised security questions (KMS, SOC2, audit logs, SSO). Agreed next steps include sharing pricing/sizing, a compatibility checklist, and ACME sending sample prompts and request traces for parity tests.

Topics: migration goals, current stack (OpenAI), model runtime preferences (vLLM/TGI), eval parity, dedicated sizing, network/VPC requirements, security/compliance

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you see my slides? I just posted the deck in the chat link -> https://redwood.ai/deck/migration-quickstart (we'll follow up with the proper link).
00:12 Sofia (CTO): Yep, got it. Thanks Jordan. Big picture: we're paying a lot on OpenAI and want more control — mainly latency/cost and some data residency needs for EU customers.
00:25 Jordan: Totally. That's the common pattern. Quick intros — Priya and Marcus are our SE duo who do the deep technical work. Can you run through the current setup and traffic profile?
00:37 Liam (ML Eng): Sure. We're primarily on GPT-4-ish models via OpenAI, plus a few Anthropic runs for chat experiments. Peak is about 80 qps across a mix of chat completions and some longer generation prompts, average seq len around 512 tokens, 95th latency target ~400 ms. We also have some batch embedding jobs for search.
01:05 Priya (SE): Ok, sounds like a workload that maps to either Redwood Hosted or Dedicated depending on SLOs and cost. When you say "GPT-4-ish", do you mean you rely on exact output parity or is functional equivalence OK?
01:18 Nina (Product): We need parity for a set of golden prompts — product experience can't change significantly. Some variance is OK, but we have tests for regressions.
01:28 Marcus (SE): That's helpful. For parity we usually run an eval harness — we can run ACME's sample prompt set against your OpenAI baseline and then against Redwood-hosted and a Dedicated deployment (with vLLM/TGI backends) to compare distributions and BLEU/embedding similarity.
01:50 Harpreet (Infra): From infra side we care about network topology — can Dedicated be VPC peered or do we need on-prem boxes? Also KMS for key management and audit logs for requests.
02:05 Priya: Dedicated supports customer VPC peering and private networking, and we have an on-prem package for air-gapped needs. KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM options) are available and we capture audit logs; we'll share SOC2 and ISO docs.
02:22 Sofia: Great. Any caveats around runtime differences — we use vLLM in-house sometimes and also TGI for certain models.
02:32 Marcus: Redwood Dedicated can orchestrate different runtimes. Some early customers run vLLM for lower-latency local Llama variants and TGI for other models; our runtime has optimizations (kv cache handling, continuous batching) that help. Important note: model artifacts and tokenizers need to be compatible. For OpenAI models we usually recommend mapping to a similar open model (e.g., Llama 2 or Mistral if appropriate) — that can change outputs.
03:03 Liam: That's the worry — if we switch model families our product tests might fail. How precise is the mapping?
03:12 Priya: It depends. For many use cases we can achieve high functional parity using curated model variants plus prompt engineering and temperature tuning. For absolute verbatim parity (i.e., identical tokens), that's unlikely unless you're running the exact same model weights. We recommend running our eval parity pipeline — it will quantify drift.
03:30 Nina: How long does the parity run take? We have a small pilot window (2 weeks).
03:36 Marcus: For a 1k prompt set it's usually 1–3 days to run full distributional comparisons if you provide the data and traces; setup might take a couple days. We can prioritize.
03:48 Jordan: On pricing — Dedicated is reserved capacity so it's a mix of committed spend and burst. We'll send a sizing spreadsheet; given 80 qps peak and 512 tokens average, rough thumb estimate is X GPUs of this class, but we'll do exact math and show you cost vs OpenAI for your pattern.
04:05 Harpreet: Latency targets — we're trying to keep 95th under 400ms. Can Dedicated meet that?
04:12 Priya: Yes, with the right GPU class and placement. We do autoscaling and can configure warm KV cache to hit SLOs. The tradeoff is cost — lower latency often needs more reserved capacity.
04:25 Sofia: Security: SOC2, SSO, SAML, RBAC, and data residency. Also retention policies — can we configure logs to be purged or kept in our account?
04:35 Marcus: We offer SSO/SAML, fine-grained RBAC, and audit logs exports. For Private/On-prem you manage retention. For Dedicated, logs can be exported to your account and retention controlled, or retained in Redwood for a configurable window per contract. We'll share the security pack.
04:56 Liam: A technical question — we use some custom tokenizers and have a custom model serving layer. How tightly coupled is Redwood to a particular tokenizer?
05:05 Priya: Tokenizer compatibility can be a sticking point. We can containerize custom tokenizers or run them in the same inference pipeline, but it's an engineering effort. For standard tokenizers (BPE, SentencePiece) it's straightforward. We should capture details in the checklist.
05:24 Jordan: Let's talk timeline: what's realistic to have a pilot?
05:28 Sofia: We have procurement cycles but want to start a technical pilot within 3–4 weeks.
05:33 Jordan: That seems doable — immediate next steps: 1) ACME shares sample prompt set + 1k request trace, 2) Redwood runs eval parity on Hosted and Dedicated estimate, 3) we share pricing + sizing, 4) follow-up technical deep dive.
05:50 Nina: Sounds good. Anything about SLA?
05:54 Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA options in enterprise package; we'll include that in the pricing doc.
06:00 Harpreet: Networking — do you support private peering to our VPC, and do we have to open egress to Redwood IPs?
06:10 Marcus: We support VPC peering and private endpoints; exact requirements depend on region. We'll provide the network checklist.
06:18 Liam: For eval parity metrics, what do you measure?
06:22 Priya: We'll report token-level similarity, embedding cosine distributions for embedding tasks, perplexity shifts, and some task-specific metrics you provide (e.g., F1, BLEU). Also sample scoring, and a qualitative comparison of failure modes.
06:40 Sofia: Any mention of vendor lock-in? We want the ability to move back to OpenAI if needed.
06:46 Jordan: Our product supports multi-routing so you can run a canary on OpenAI while most traffic goes to Dedicated — fallback policies are supported. That reduces lock-in risk.
06:58 Nina: Are there customers who migrated recently we can talk to?
07:02 Jordan: Yes, we'll share references — particularly those who moved from OpenAI to Dedicated for cost predictability.
07:08 Harpreet: One more on compliance — do you support customer-managed keys (bring your own key)?
07:13 Marcus: Yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations is supported in Private and for certain Dedicated plans. We'll note limits in the security doc.
07:24 Liam: Cool. We also run some heavy batch embedding pipelines — is there a recommendation to separate that onto different pools?
07:32 Priya: Yes, we typically recommend separating latency-sensitive small requests from large batch embedding workloads to optimize cost — different instance classes and batching configs.
07:42 Jordan: Alright let's recap and owners: Jordan will send pricing and sizing; Priya will run compatibility checklist and sample eval; ACME (Liam) will upload prompt set and traces. We'll schedule follow up deep dive with Harpreet and infra.
07:58 Sofia: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity. We'll aim to get the artifacts over this week.
08:03 Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and calendar invite for the deep dive.

Notes / Links shared: Redwood migration deck (https://redwood.ai/deck/migration-quickstart), Dedicated sizing template (shared via email), security pack (SOC2/ISO) promised.

End of transcript.
